item.title: Iran conflict could ‘bring down the economies of the world,’ warns one of the Middle East’s biggest energy exporters
item.description: One of the most important names in the global natural gas trade says the war will send a “chain reaction” rippling through the world.

item.title: Gen Z graduates who majored in ‘AI-proof’ careers like pharmacy, biology, and education are making less than $50,000 after graduation
item.description: Gen Z workers are flocking to industries like healthcare and education in hopes of evading AI and recessionary impacts—but some of those jobs pay rock-bottom salaries.

item.title: CBO highlights the good news in Trump’s lost tariff revenue hiking the deficit by $2 trillion: Lower inflation and unemployment—and higher GDP
item.description: In the past year, tariffs were, at least partly, responsible for 166,000 lost blue-collar jobs and $1,700 in annual increased costs for American households.

item.title: Warren Buffett’s successor is all-in on the company: He will spend his entire after-tax salary of $15M buying Berkshire Hathaway stock
item.description: Berkshire is also resuming share buybacks, despite Buffett’s previous aversion.

item.title: A Minneapolis Fed report details how much Trump’s immigration crackdown hurt businesses and workers: ‘There are not any people to hire’
item.description: “We are hiring now to replace these workers or get more reliable alternatives, but there are not any people to hire.”

item.title: Silicon Valley investor Vinod Khosla predicts education will be free, and the future of college is ‘a real question’
item.description: The billionaire VC says AI raises questions about how we value expertise.

item.title: February was the biggest month in venture history, thanks to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Waymo in particular
item.description: Startup funding surged to a historic $189 billion in February, driven almost entirely by three AI mega-rounds that captured 83% of the total.

item.title: OpenAI investor Vinod Khosla believes AI will be able to do 80% of all jobs by 2030. Here’s how life could be affordable after mass unemployment
item.description: The Silicon Valley billionaire foresees a deflationary economy—but also free health care and education, along with a tax overhaul.

item.title: Palmer Luckey says Silicon Valley has the Pentagon all wrong: ‘Stick to a position that this is in the hands of the people’
item.description: Luckey said that allowing tech companies to decide how to use AI effectively transfers power from the U.S. government to corporations.

item.title: Nobel laureate Joe Stiglitz says not only can AI take your job, it’ll make the ‘tech bro’ class richer while doing so
item.description: “Unfortunately, the tech bros, who are obviously advocates of this, are at the same time pushing for smaller government,” Stiglitz told Fortune.
